results.reasoning: Judged by driving a scratch copy of this blueprint served from inside itself, and a second copy placed outside any repository, reading each spec_hash out of a record walkdown itself wrote. Baseline sha256:9cf589d6656b. Writing a verdict, a note (n-0184) and a draft (drafts/local.json) left it at sha256:9cf589d6656b and touched no file under blueprint/; a one-word rewording moved it to sha256:21b106f8bfb7 and restoring the bytes brought it back; edits to storyboard.yml and walkdown.yml moved it too, while trailing whitespace and extra blank lines at EOF correctly did not, and a two-space re-indent did (sha256:63682ec4fde5). For the third clause I renamed features/locations.yml to locations2.yml with byte-identical content and an unchanged sort position: sha256:54ed9bb1731d, so the path really is inside the hash, and cutting the rule into panel.yml gave a third value again. Served from a directory with no git above it, the record carried no git_sha and no tree_hash yet the same sha256:9cf589d6656b, so a verdict says what it measured with or without a repository. Sweeps and both check reporters stamp it too. One gap I could not resolve into a fail of these steps but which undercuts the statement's 'every run': nothing enforces the field, RUN_SHAPE ignores it, and 67 agent-written walkdown records in this ledger - including the ten written earlier in this sitting - have no spec_hash at all. Filed as n-0189. Two smaller observations: blueprint/AGENTS.md is outside specFiles(), and the per-file feed is unprefixed so a collision is theoretically constructible but not in valid YAML.
